evidence.curator_note: ARCS ACTUALLY DRAWN: ZERO. Equation 8.116 consists of three structures joined by two double-headed EQUILIBRIUM arrows; no curved arrow or fishhook is drawn, so all three moves of this step are curator-constructed (they are the canonical three-fishhook radical ring closure: the C1 radical electron into the forming C1-C3 bond, one electron of the C3=O pi bond into that same forming bond, and the second pi electron onto oxygen, which is where the book's '+.' sits on the cyclic structure). WHAT THE PAGE DRAWS: '.CH2CH2CH=+OH' on the left, the cyclopropane ring with a 'CHOH' apex and '+.' written outside the structure in the middle, and 'H+O=CHCH2CH2.' on the right. The middle structure is drawn by the book, so it is encoded as a genuine intermediate state rather than an invention. Convention B/C: the book leaves the charge and odd electron of the cyclic ion unlocalised ('+.' outside the ring); they are localised here on the hydroxyl oxygen (O+. with two bonds), the n-ionised cyclopropanol form, so that the arrows have a real origin and terminus.

ARCS ACTUALLY DRAWN: ZERO (see the first step). The right-hand structure the book prints, 'H+O=CHCH2CH2.', is the SAME connectivity as the left-hand one written in the opposite direction: the point of Equation 8.116 is that ring closure and re-opening of the OTHER ring bond permutes the two methylene groups, i.e. the interconversion is degenerate. That permutation is what the atom maps record here: the ring opens at C2-C3 instead of C1-C3, so the radical ends up on C2 while the carbon skeleton is unchanged. Three fishhooks, the exact reverse of step 1.

NO MØD RULE IS CROSS-LINKED, and this was CHECKED, not assumed (convention E). rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no '8.116' key at all -- its chapter-8 index runs 8.1-8.14 only (German-edition numbering), so nothing in src/data_generation/rules/ is authored for this equation. Nor is there any isomerisation rule in the set: every fragmentation rule in src/data_generation/rules/ takes a bond apart and the ionisation rules only add a charge/radical, so a degenerate ring-closure/ring-opening interconversion (no change in formula, charge or unpaired-electron count) has no representative to test.

NO MEASUREMENT ON THE PAGE (convention F): Equation 8.116 prints no m/z and no abundance -- it is a structural interconversion scheme only. m/z 58.0413 is the curator-computed monoisotopic mass of C3H6O+. and is recorded with status 'inferred', detected=false and no relative_intensity. All three species have the same m/z, so no ion is distinguishable by mass here.
